Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 106, verse 1–4:

Tafsir of Surah Li'ilaf Quraysh (The Covenant of Quraysh)

It is Meccan.

Mention of a rare hadith concerning its virtue: al-Bayhaqi said in his book "al-Khilafiyyat": Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz narrated to us, Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Sayrafi narrated to us in Marw, Ahmad ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Narsi [In M, A, H: "al-Zaynabi", which is an error.] narrated to us, Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Thabit ibn Shurahbil narrated to us, 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah [ibn] [Addition from M, A.] Abi 'Atiq narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn 'Amr ibn Ja'dah ibn Hubayrah, from his father, from his grandmother Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has favoured Quraysh with seven distinctions: that I am from them, that prophethood is among them, the custodianship of the Ka'bah (al-Hijabah) and the provision of water to pilgrims (al-Siqayah) are among them, that Allah gave them victory over the Elephant, that they worshipped Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for ten years, with none other worshipping Him, and that Allah sent down among them a surah of the Qur'an." Then the Messenger of Allah recited: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. For the covenant of Quraysh, their covenant of the caravan of winter and summer, let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear." [Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in Manaqib al-Shafi'i (1/34), and it is in al-Mustadrak (2/536). Al-Hakim said: "Its chain is sahih, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." Al-Dhahabi criticised this, saying: "In it is Ya'qub ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri, who is weak, and Ibrahim is one who narrates munkar reports, which he denied." The Hafiz al-'Iraqi graded this hadith as hasan. Shaykh Nasir al-Din al-Albani has a discussion on this hadith in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah under no. (1944), in which he went to grade it as hasan, and Allah knows best.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

This surah is separated from the one before it in the Imam Mushaf; they wrote between them a line of "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful," even though it is connected to what precedes it. This is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam stated, because the meaning according to them is: We withheld the Elephant from Makkah and destroyed its people. "For the covenant of Quraysh" means: for their coming together and gathering in their land, secure.

It was also said: what is meant is what they were accustomed to of the journey in winter to Yemen and in summer to Syria for trade and other purposes, and then they returned to their land secure in their travels, because of their greatness among people, as they were the inhabitants of Allah's sacred sanctuary; whoever knew them respected them, and whoever attached himself to them and travelled with them was secured by them. This was their condition during their journeys and their winter and summer travels. As for their state when they were settled in the land, Allah said: "Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are snatched away from around them?" [Al-'Ankabut: 67]. For this reason He said: "For the covenant of Quraysh" as a substitute for the first and as its explanation. For this reason He said: "their covenant of the caravan of winter and summer."

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the "lam" is the lam of wonder, as if He is saying: Marvel at the covenant of Quraysh and My favour upon them in that. He said: This is because the Muslims have agreed that they are two separate, independent surahs. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/198).]

Then He guided them to thank this great blessing, saying: "So let them worship the Lord of this House," meaning: let them single Him out in worship, as He made for them a secure sanctuary and a sacred House, as Allah the Exalted said: "I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which He has made sacred, and to whom all things belong, and I have been commanded to be among the Muslims." [Al-Naml: 91]

* *

His saying: "who has fed them against hunger" means: He is the Lord of the House, and He is "who has fed them against hunger and secured them against fear," meaning: He bestowed upon them security and ease. So let them single Him out in worship alone, with no partner, and let them not worship besides Him any idol, rival or false god. For this reason, whoever responds to this command, Allah combines for him the security of this world and the security of the Hereafter, and whoever disobeys Him, He strips both from him, as Allah the Exalted said: "And Allah presents a parable: a town that was secure and at rest, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the blessings of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do. And there came to them a Messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers." [Al-Nahl: 112-113]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr al-'Adani narrated to us, Qabisah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Woe to your mother, O Quraysh, for the covenant of Quraysh!" [Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (24/177, 178) through the route of Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah, from Sufyan, with the same chain.] Then he said:

My father narrated to us, al-Mu'ammal ibn al-Fadl al-Harrani narrated to us, 'Isa, meaning Ibn Yunus, narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "For the covenant of Quraysh, their covenant of the caravan of winter and summer. Woe to you, O assembly of Quraysh, worship the Lord of this House, who has fed you against hunger and secured you against fear."

Thus I saw it from Usamah ibn Zayd, but its correct form is from Asma' bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan, Umm Salamah al-Ansariyyah, may Allah be pleased with her. [And so it is in the narration of Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/460), from 'Ali ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn Yunus, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, from the Prophet (ﷺ).] So perhaps an error occurred in the copy or in the original narration, and Allah knows best.

End of the tafsir of Surah "Li'ilaf Quraysh".
